historical_basis.quote: Apsaras (Sanskrit: अप्सरस्, IAST: Apsaras, Khmer: អប្សរា, Pali: अच्छरा, romanized: Accharā, Thai: อัปสร) are a class of celestial beings in Hindu and Buddhist culture. They were originally a type of female spirit associated with clouds and water, but, later came to play the role of a "nymph" or "fairy".

statement.id: Apsara adalah kelompok makhluk perempuan surgawi dalam tradisi Hindu dan Buddha.
statement.en: Apsaras are a class of celestial female beings in Hindu and Buddhist traditions.

historical_basis.quote: The apsaras are described as being beautiful, youthful and elegant, and are said to be able to change their shape at will; making anyone fall for their beauty. There are two types of apsaras—laukika (worldly) and daivika (divine). They are said to excel at dancing, and are often considered the wives of the gandharvas, the court musicians of Indra.

statement.id: Mereka dikenal sebagai penari istana Indra.
statement.en: They are known as dancers at Indra's court.

historical_basis.quote: The Monier-Williams et al. (1899) gives the etymology as अप् + √सृ, "going in the waters or between the waters of the clouds".

statement.id: Etimologi Monier-Williams menghubungkan namanya dengan bergerak di air atau di antara air awan.
statement.en: Monier Williams's etymology connects the name with moving in water or among cloud waters.

historical_basis.quote: The Kaushitaki Upanishad mentions apsaras as a class of divinities associated with ointments, garlands, vestments, and powdered aromatics.

statement.id: Kaushitaki Upanishad mengaitkan apsara dengan minyak wangi, rangkaian bunga, pakaian, dan wewangian bubuk.
statement.en: The Kaushitaki Upanishad associates apsaras with ointments, garlands, clothes, and powdered aromatics.
